note: A rendered memo's snapshot `<memo>.tetel/` ships exactly 9 enumerated files, including `prose.jsonl` and `claims.jsonl` (SNAPSHOT_FILES). So prose-block and claim event logs — with their timestamps — travel beside the memo and are readable by `check`. Evidence records live separately in `<memo>.evidence.jsonl` (crate::evidence), not in the snapshot. Also: `render` writes prose, `*cites: …*` markers and a claim ledger and nothing else — a fact's captured extent never appears in the document, which is why snapshot-dependent findings (notes_outside_extent, mint_windows) exist as a class.

Two facts about identity and ordering inside the authoring workspace. (1) compose::render emits, per prose block, the block's text and — for a paragraph with citations — a `*cites: C…*` marker; the block's own id (P#) is never written into the document. The evidence ledger it appends uses the workspace claim ids verbatim (`ledger_cell(&c.id)`), so a rendered ledger id and a workspace claim id are the same string. (2) claims.rs: ClaimEvent::Create/Revise/Withdraw each carry `timestamp: u64` from workspace::now_unix(), but claims::load_all discards them, exposing only `revisions: usize`. prose.rs's ProseEvent::Create/Revise likewise each carry `timestamp: u64` and load_all discards them, exposing only `revisions: usize`. So both timestamps exist in the shipped jsonl logs and no loader currently surfaces them.

prose.rs lines 41-123: ProseEvent::Create carries id, heading, level, text, cite, before, timestamp: u64; ProseEvent::Revise carries id, text, why, cite: Option<Vec<String>>, timestamp: u64. A Revise with `cite: None` leaves the block's citations untouched, so a revision need not restate them. prose::load_all replays the log into Block { id, heading, level, text, cite, revisions: usize } and drops every timestamp — no caller can see when a block's current text was authored without re-reading prose.jsonl. Document order is the replayed insertion order (`before` anchors), not event order.

The proposed rule, executed against the two shipped memos' own snapshots and evidence logs. Rule as run: a non-heading prose block with a non-empty cite list is reported iff every cited id resolves to a ledger claim, every one of those claims is in proof (some record's digest equals sha256 of its current proposition), and the block's current-text timestamp (Create, or last Revise) is strictly greater than the MAXIMUM over cited claims of that claim's EARLIEST in-proof record timestamp.

Result on the real data: tet28 (20 blocks, 15 claims, all 15 in proof) reports 0; tet29 (12 blocks, 14 claims, all 14 in proof) reports 0.

Why zero, checked against the logs rather than assumed. tet28 has 15 prose revisions; the two post-grounding ones (P2 at 1786132471 "C1 was narrowed after grounding pass k1 qualified its 'clean working tree' clause", P18 at 1786132480 "C13 was narrowed after grounding pass k1 qualified its universal…") each accompanied a claim revision, so the new wording's first proof (pass k2, ~1786133xxx) postdates the prose edit and the rule correctly stays silent. Its last six revisions (t=1786135098, after the last first-proof at 1786134045) are all heading blocks — a markdown-prefix fix — and headings are outside the rule. tet29's post-grounding revision (P4 at 1786174635, "C4 was revised after k1 qualified it") is excluded the same way: C4's new digest 1c542cfe first entered proof at 1786175367.

note: A whole-worktree grep of /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel for `fn now_unix` finds exactly two definitions: evidence.rs:288 and workspace.rs:257. Both are byte-equivalent — `SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_secs()).unwrap_or(0)` — so a prose/claim event timestamp (workspace clock) and an evidence record timestamp (whatever process wrote the record) are the same unit and the same epoch, UTC seconds, with no timezone term. What they are not is the same clock: `SystemTime::now()` reads the wall clock of the process that calls it, and nothing in either function or in the record shape ties the two processes together. Note also workspace.rs's separate `ts()` used for refusals.log, which formats the same value as a decimal string.

evidence.rs lines 128-216, the whole record shape. A Statement is {_type, subject: Vec<Subject>, predicateType, predicate}; Subject is {name, digest: DigestSet{sha256}} — one sha256, and it is of the claim proposition; Predicate is {verdict, pass, reported_kind, source, extent, world, note, pin, timestamp}. There is no field anywhere in the record that names or digests a prose block, and RecordInput — the entire ingestion surface a reporter can fill — has no such field either. The only digest a grounding pass writes is over the proposition it was briefed on.

The cost of a whole-worktree census in this repository, measured. The two shipped memos' snapshots already carry large captures: tet29's facts.jsonl is 11 lines / 116734 bytes with a longest line of 57110 bytes, tet28's 10 lines / 127314 bytes with a longest line of 34412 — a fact's captured output is one JSON line, so a snapshot holds whole file dumps on single lines. Counting, over every non-binary file in the worktree, the lines containing each symbol this design must modify: `render` 486 lines / 373271 bytes (longest line 57249); `Findings` 23 lines / 57418 bytes (longest 27190); `NON_COVERAGE` 35 lines / 95637 bytes (longest 27190); `check_file` 5 lines / 285 bytes. So the census of a common symbol in this repo costs a few hundred kilobytes of captured output, and most of that weight is the previous memos' own snapshots being re-captured. Bounded and payable, but it grows with every memo the repo accumulates.

note:
Two observations behind the attack findings.

(1) prose.rs lines 172-202, `revise`: it refuses only on an unknown block id and an empty `--why`. It never compares `new_text` to the block's existing text, and it writes `cite` straight through — so a revision that restates byte-identical text while replacing the citation list is an ordinary, unrefused act. The doc comment says why the `cite` parameter exists: without it "a paragraph created without a citation could never be given one ... which made `tetel review`'s own instruction ('mint the missing claim and cite it') unreachable for existing prose." So a citation-only revision is not merely permitted, it is the act the tool added the parameter to permit.

(2) ledger.rs lines 70-140, `split_row_cells`: it `trim()`s the whole line, un-escapes `\|` back to `|`, respects backtick spans, and `trim()`s every cell it emits. So a ledger cell round-trips a pipe but not leading or trailing whitespace, and — since a markdown row is one physical line — not an embedded newline either.

Two observations, folded into one mint.

(1) lib.rs lines 85-100: `check_file` builds its claim list as `ledger::import(&doc.body)` — from the parsed rendered document — and passes exactly those claims to both `checks::analyze` and `checks::analyze_ledger`. It never opens the snapshot's `claims.jsonl`. So the propositions every `proposition_digest` on record was computed over are the ledger-derived ones, and any check reusing the in-proof predicate must take its claims from `ledger::import`, not from `claims.jsonl`.

(2) Executing the attack's three constructions against tet29's real logs, under the rule as it stood and under a two-part repair. Under the old rule (block timestamp = earliest event bearing the current text; every cited claim required in proof): the baseline fix-round rewrite of P11 at 1786174700 is listed against anchor 1786174494, and all three escapes silence it — a citation-only revision adding the already-in-proof C4, a citation-only revision adding a record-less C99, and the dual (an old uncited paragraph P2 given a citation to a settled claim) all produce NOTHING LISTED. Under the repair — block timestamp = earliest event whose text AND citation list both equal the current ones, and the in-proof gate changed from "every cited claim" to "at least one cited claim, with the anchor taken over the in-proof ones" — the baseline is still listed, escape A is listed (P11, ts 1786176500, anchor 1786175367, cites C13+C4), escape B is listed (ts 1786176500, anchor 1786174494), the dual is listed (P2, ts 1786176500, anchor 1786174494), and the untouched memo still lists nothing.
